Alkylation units are what boost the gasoline’s octane level when the process stream leaves the distillation unit. All gasoline is the same up until it leaves the alkylation unit. The previous poster is correct gasoline is blended at the terminal and either loaded into trucks at the refinery(this is where a refinery like shell puts the additive package into their branded gas) or is piped to another terminal where the additives are put in. When you crack a barrel of oil you’re gonna get the same amount of gas no matter what(for the sake of simplicity please ignore FCC units). So if the refinery decides there is little demand for high octane blends they’ll cut back the alky unit production to the bare minimum necessary for unleaded. They have to do something with the gasoline they cracked though so once storage fills up they start dumping it cheaply. However the higher octane gas is a special blend that they can turn off and this would mean there’s even more unleaded available for shipment. For those people that are dumb enough to buy mid grade unnecessarily or have vehicles requiring premium the oil companies know they have a captive market and aren’t going to cut their profits by putting out more of the high octane gas. They’re just going to put out an increased amount of unleaded hence why the unleaded price is falling.
